title: Order-invariant measures on causal sets
assumptions: Order-invariant measures on causal-set growth processes; at fixed finite step, conditional on finite order structure, possible generation orders equiprobable.
conclusion: Connects order-invariant measures and causal-set growth, explicitly identifying fixed-step conditional uniformity with Rideout–Sorkin general covariance; classifies extremal measures.
proof_status: Full text read for cited sections; extremal classification not audited.
dependencies: Countable causal-set growth process with natural extensions; finite-step conditional distributions.
relevance: Direct prior art for stopping-stage ancillarity and conditional uniformity.
limits: Does not state our arbitrary adapted stopping-time count formula as a separate named theorem; that formula follows by finite counting from order-invariance.
open_questions: The source addresses fixed-step order-invariance; the stopping-time formula here is only its finite counting consequence, not a separate result attributed to the authors.

title: A manifestly covariant framework for causal set dynamics
assumptions: Countable past-finite causal sets; covariant event algebra generated (up to rogue null sets in CSG) by stems; random walk on covtree for a classical measure.
conclusion: Builds a manifestly label-independent covtree framework; classical random-walk transition probabilities induce a measure on the stem sigma-algebra.
proof_status: Full text read for framework, definitions, and dynamic construction; appendices not audited.
dependencies: Past-finite causal-set path space, covariant event definitions, and the CSG result that rogues are null.
relevance: Defeats the claim that a path-free covariant event algebra or observer access requires a new quotient construction.
limits: Does not specify a physically marked observer with internal memory or a matter Bell-causality extension.
open_questions: How should physically marked observer records or matter states be incorporated while satisfying a nontrivial local causality condition?

title: Order-invariant measures on fixed causal sets
assumptions: Measures on natural extensions of a fixed countable past-finite causal set; order-invariance conditioned on the set of the bottom k elements.
conclusion: Gives sufficient conditions for existence and uniqueness of order-invariant measures on fixed causal sets.
proof_status: Abstract/version metadata read; body not audited.
relevance: Nearby prior work on random natural extensions of fixed causal sets.
limits: Not used for a theorem claim in this note.

title: Finite Markov Chains
locators: Theorem 6.3.2 (lumpability criterion; locator surfaced by primary literature/search results, monograph not obtained for direct audit)
assumptions: Finite-state Markov chain and a partition into blocks.
conclusion: Strong lumpability is characterized by equal transition probability into each target block from every state in a source block.
relevance: Generic prior art for Markov/non-Markov behavior under forgetting a hidden mark.
limits: Not relied on for causal-set claims; no direct text verification this pass.

title: Observables for cyclic causal set cosmologies
assumptions: Sequential growth on labeled causal sets; principal-cylinder-generated reduced poscau for infinitely many breaks and doubly-principal-cylinder-generated doubly-reduced poscau for infinitely many posts; complex transitive-percolation amplitude A(C)=p^L(1-p)^(binom(n,2)-R). Extension criterion applies to a finite-valency tree with no maximal elements.
conclusion: Defines the reduced and doubly-reduced observable trees; gives complex-premeasure extension criteria via level variation sums. For reduced poscau it numerically checks levels 2–4 and conjectures eventual minimum ζ_n^min=|p|+|1-p|-1. For doubly-reduced poscau it explicitly says the criterion is inconclusive because levels contain valency-one nodes with ζ=0; suggests eventual behavior numerically but leaves extension unresolved.
proof_status: Full text read for cited sections. The exact principal-gadget enumeration and repetition lower bound in this report are independent checks, not results attributed to the authors.
dependencies: Complex transitive-percolation path amplitudes; sigma-algebras generated by principal and doubly-principal cylinder nodes; the finite-valency-tree complex-measure extension criterion.
relevance: Closest direct predecessor and strongest novelty defeater for the bounded reduced-algebra no-extension candidate.
limits: Does not prove the present all-level repeated-block lower bound or settle a measure defined only on the covariant intersection algebra. The paper’s broader numerical evidence could make the parameter-specific proof unsurprising; global priority search is unverified.
open_questions: Could exact concatenation bounds prove nonextension for other complex parameters? Does a measure exist on the covariant intersection alone? Are there later results beyond the numerical evidence in §V?

title: A Criterion for Covariance in Complex Sequential Growth Models
locators: §§2–3, especially Theorem 2.1 and complex transitive-percolation variation analysis
assumptions: Complex premeasure on the labeled cylinder algebra of sequential causal-set growth; extension to the generated sigma-algebra requires bounded variation.
conclusion: Proves an extension criterion for complex measures and shows complex transitive percolation extends to the full labeled-history sigma-algebra iff p is real in [0,1]. Discusses covariant/stem-event limits but does not establish extension on reduced or doubly-reduced poscau.
proof_status: Full text read for extension criterion and relevant complex-percolation sections.
dependencies: Finite-valency tree structure of labeled poscau; complex transitive-percolation amplitudes.
relevance: Primary predecessor for full-algebra complex measure extension and bounded variation.
limits: Its full labeled-history criterion does not decide extension on the smaller labeled cyclic-observable trees or their covariant intersections.
open_questions: The source discusses conditional convergence for selected covariant events; whether a measure extends to a smaller physically motivated covariant algebra is not settled by its full-sigma result.

title: On extending the Quantum Measure
locators: §2, Claims 1–2, arXiv HTML lines 125–154; §4, complex percolation lemma and variation argument, lines 244–300 and 375–376
assumptions: Strongly-positive quantum measure represented by a histories-Hilbert-space-valued vector premeasure; extension to the generated sigma-algebra requires countable additivity and hence bounded variation. Complex percolation uses p+q=1 and labeled finite-causet cylinder amplitudes.
conclusion: Relates extension of the quantum measure/decoherence functional to extension of its vector-measure avatar; proves the complex-percolation vector premeasure fails to extend to the full labeled-history sigma algebra when p is nonreal. It discusses the role of covariant observables but does not establish extension on reduced or doubly-reduced poscau.
proof_status: Full text read for the stated sections; vector-measure construction and bounded-variation necessity checked. No claim here that it settles smaller observable algebras.
dependencies: Histories Hilbert-space construction from a strongly-positive decoherence functional; standard bounded-variation facts for finite-dimensional vector measures.
relevance: Primary predecessor for complex measure/vector-measure extension and the nonextension result on the full labeled causal-set history algebra.
limits: Its bounded-variation proof is for the full labeled event algebra. It does not imply failure on a smaller algebra generated only by covariant records.
open_questions: Can a complex quantum measure extend on a physically motivated smaller covariant algebra even where the full labeled sigma-algebra extension fails? The paper raises this general issue but does not answer the reduced-poscau question.
